newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S B BAND AREA NO.2 SEEN DRAWING BIG PREMIUM.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S B BAND AREA NO.2 SEEN DRAWING BIG PREMIUM.

text.p: Investors are likely to offer huge premiums of at least 100 percent during bidding Friday for the right to operate cellular services in non-metropolitan Sao Paulo state, bank analysts said Thursday.
"It's a very attractive area," said Vera Rossi of ING Barings in Sao Paulo. "It's a wealthy area and has a large population."

To be sure, the auction for the B Band Area No.2 license is not expected to match last month's 2.64 billion real ($2.45 billion) bid by BCP SA group for Area No.1, covering Sao Paulo city, a 333 percent premium to the base price.

Still, for Area No.2, analysts are forecasting a huge premium -- ranging from 100 percent to 200 percent -- to the government-set minimum price of 600 million reais, the same base price set for Area No.1.
"It's the second-best area in the country after Sao Paulo city," said Claudio Nassur of Fonte Cindam.

Area No.2 is home to 17 million people, roughly the same population as the Sao Paulo metropolitan area, but is not as wealthy and does not have the massive pent-up demand of the city, where waiting lists of telephone service are long, analysts said.
Bids from four groups are expected to be opened Friday. The groups are:
--TT-2 Telecomunicacoes, made up of Brazil's Bradesco bank and Globo Participacoes, AT&T Corp of the United States and Italy's Stet SpA.
--Brascom, comprised of Andrade Gutierrez and Monteiro Aranha, both Brazil; Southwestern Bell, a unit of SBC Communications Inc and Mannesmann Eurokom of Germany.
--Avantel, made up of Odebrecht and Camargo Correa, Unibanco bank and U.S-based AirTouch Communications Inc.
--Global Telecom, made up of Suzano and Inepar of Brazil, DDI Corp and Nissho Iwai Corp of Japan, and Motorola Inc of the United States.
Analysts said the favorites to win the license are TT-2 and Avantel, which placed second and third, respectively, in the Area No.1 bidding on July 9.
The BCP group, which includes BellSouth Corp and Brazil's Banco Safra, dropped its Area No.2 bid after winning Area No.1.
Offers from two other groups were declared ineligible by the government. The consortia -- Telet SA and Tess -- are both appealing through Brazilian courts.

The Communications Ministry also will open bids for B Band Area No.10, covering the rural northeastern states of Alagoas, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco and Piaui. The government has set a 230 million-real base price for that concession.
Areas No.2 and No.10 will be the fourth and fifth B Band licenses granted in its privatization of the country's cellular telephone sector.

Apart from Sao Paulo city, the government has granted contracts for rural Area No.7, comprising central-western Brazil and the federal district of Brasilia, and Area No.9, made up of Bahia and Sergipe states.
